_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The EPA RMP regulation requires that an Executive Summary be provided as part of the registration submitted to the EPA. 
Note: This summary includes additional information not included in the RMP Submit to assist SupHerb Farms management, process operators, technicians, contractors plus all involved and affected employees towards safe operation. In addition, some of the detail provided within this summary was excluded from the submitted RMP as current public access to this detail could expose the facility and personnel to terrorist or criminal activity.

SupHerb Farms prepared a Chemical Risk Management Program and Process Safety Management Program (RMP/PSM) in general accordance with state and federal regulations. The state risk management regulations, also referred to as the California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) program, are codified in California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 19, Section 2745, et. seq. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) also regulates facilities with certain toxic and flammable substances. The federal regulations are codified in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Title 40, Section 68. Finally, both the California Occupational Safety and Health Administration (CalOSHA) and the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulate facilities with certain acutely hazardous materials under the PSM standards as defined in CCR, Title 8, Section 5189 and CFR Title 29, Part 1910, Section 119, respectively.

The following areas are addressed in this summary:
1.	Accidental release prevention and emergency response policies 
2.	The stationary source and regulated substances handled
3.	The accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps
4.	The five-year accident history
5.	The emergency response program
6.	Planned changes to improve safety

C-1   ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES 

SupHerb Farms is committed to complying with all the regulatory requirements of

the EPA Risk Management Program.  SupHerb Farms has developed their Risk Management Plan / Process Safety Management (RMP/PSM) making up the CalARP program to document policies and address the implementation of these regulations. The PSM sections pertain to the prevention of accidental releases and include the Process Hazard Analysis study and procedures for operating, training, maintenance, emergency response, and others. The RMP sections pertain to management systems and include the Hazard Assessment (Offsite Consequence Analysis) Report.

In the unlikely event that a chemical release does occur at the facility, SupHerb Farms personnel are trained in the appropriate mitigation measures, relying on emergency services provided by local response agencies. SupHerb Farms will continue to improve ammonia-handling safety through the implementation of the prevention program elements of the RMP/PSM program.

C-2   STATIONARY SOURCE ACTIVITIES AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES HANDLED

SupHerb Farms is located at 300 Dianne Drive, Turlock, California. The area is zoned for industrial use. This facility processes herbs and specialty vegetables by freezing and/or other processing. Fresh herbs and specialty vegetables are processed through an Instant Quick Freeze (IQF) tunnel. Frozen herbs are packaged for wholesale markets or processed through a paste line. Cold storage is also provided within the warehouse for holding packaged final products.

Anhydrous ammonia (CAS No. 7664-41-7) is the regulated substance used in the facility's refrigeration system. The refrigeration system, which is a closed system, contains approximately 19,300 pounds of anhydrous ammonia. The system provides cooling to the cold storage rooms, and processing lines. The cold rooms are used to store finished products ready for shipping.

Chlorine (CAS No. 7782-50-5) is utilized as a biocide to disinfect the process water in the facility which is used in three wash lines. The source of chlorine for the chlorination

system during normal operation is a ton container. Two (2) ton containers may be on site, resulting in a maximum chlorine inventory of 4,000 pounds. At times 150 Lb. bottles are used when the ton cylinders are running low.

C-3	RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM

To minimize the potential for accidental releases, SupHerb Farms has implemented a comprehensive prevention program consistent with the elements required under RMP,  CalARP, and PSM regulations. Key components include:

	Process Safety Information (PSI):
Complete and accurate written information is maintained on the hazardous properties of regulated substances, the design basis and configuration of process equipment, and the technology of the processes. This information is used as a foundation for safe operation and hazard evaluation.

	Process Hazard Analysis (PHA):
A thorough hazard analysis is conducted for each covered process using approved methodologies (e.g., What-If/Checklist, HAZOP, FMEA). PHA studies are updated and revalidated at least every five years. Recommendations are prioritized, tracked, and resolved.

	Operating Procedures:
Written procedures are maintained and reviewed annually for all operations including startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, and normal shutdown. These procedures ensure consistent and safe process operation.

	Training:
Operators and maintenance personnel receive initial and refresher training on process safety, operating procedures, and emergency response. Training effectiveness is verified through testing or demonstration of competency.

	Mechanical Integrity:
Critical process equipment, including pressure vessels, piping systems, relief devices, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and sensors, is subject to a preventive maintenance program. Equipment is inspected and tested following recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices (RAGAGEP).

	Management of Change (MOC):
Changes to process chemicals, technology, equipment,

procedures, or facilities are evaluated for potential safety impacts before implementation. The MOC system includes requirements for authorization, documentation, and training of affected personnel.

	Pre-startup Safety Review (PSSR):
Prior to startup of new or modified equipment/processes, a safety review is performed to ensure that construction is in accordance with design specifications, procedures are in place, training is completed, and recommendations from PHAs and MOCs are addressed.

	Compliance Audits:
A comprehensive compliance audit is conducted at least every three years to evaluate the effectiveness of the prevention program. Deficiencies identified during the audit are promptly corrected and documented. Note: This is not a PSM requirement; this is addressed in the IIPP.

	Incident Investigation:
All incidents that resulted in or could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release are investigated. The root cause is identified, and corrective actions are developed, implemented, and communicated to affected personnel.

	Employee Participation:
Employees are actively involved in the development and implementation of the prevention program. The written participation plan ensures timely access to relevant safety information and involvement in PHAs and other safety activities.

	Hot Work Permits:
A formal permitting system is used for hot work operations conducted on or near covered processes. Permits are issued only after fire prevention and protection measures are confirmed to be in place.

	Contractor Safety Management:
Contractors who work on or near covered processes are evaluated for safety performance, informed of process hazards, and trained on applicable emergency response and safe work practices. Contractor activities are monitored to ensure compliance with safety policies.

C-4	FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

The CalARP regulations require a review of the 5-year accident history at the regulated facility. History must include "all accident

al releases from covered processes that resulted in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage onsite, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage." SupHerb Farms assured no reportable release of ammonia or chlorine has occurred during the past 5 years (2020-2025).

C-5	EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

SupHerb Farms maintains a written Emergency Response Plan (ERP) as directed by the UPA. The facility only takes defensive actions for an incidental release in order to protect employees, environment and property. This plan is designed to ensure a prompt, coordinated, and effective response to accidental releases of regulated substances. Key features include:

	Emergency Planning and Coordination: Coordination with local emergency response agencies, including the local fire department and hazmat team, and other relevant authorities.

	Notification Procedures: Clearly defined procedures for immediate notification of appropriate emergency responders, the public (if necessary), and regulatory agencies in accordance with applicable release reporting requirements.

	Response Procedures: Guidance for personnel response actions, including evacuation and mitigation procedures.

	Training and Drills: Designated emergency response personnel are trained in accordance with OSHA HAZWOPER (29 CFR 1910.120) and applicable state standards. Drills and exercises are conducted to test and improve the plans effectiveness.

	Emergency Equipment: Adequate response equipment is maintained, routinely inspected, and readily available for use by trained personnel.

SupHerb Farms will rely on outside responders from the fire department and the Stanislaus County HazMat Team for mitigation of releases. The ERP states that the SupHerb Farms Emergency Coordinator will be in charge until such time as an outside responding agency assumes that role. SupHerb Farms management will oversee evacuation and remain in control until the F

ire Department arrives, then Incident Command will be assumed by the senior Fire Department official at the scene. The Fire Department Incident Commander will be responsible for issuing notices for public evacuation and/or sheltering in place, if necessary. SupHerb Farms management will be responsible for making initial contact with the Fire Department via 9-1-1; Stanislaus County UPA; CalOES, federal NRC, and any other agencies that need to be contacted. SupHerb Farms will rely on community responders for medical assistance as necessary. Responsibility for cleanup after the release is spelled out in the ERP.

C-6	PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

SupHerb Farms is dedicated to continuous improvement of its accidental release prevention and emergency preparedness programs. We actively evaluate new regulatory developments, industry best practices, audit results, and incident learnings to ensure that our policies remain effective, current, and protective of our employees, community, and environment. Management responses and support will be consistent with SupHerb Farms's commitment to safe and environmentally responsible operations.

SupHerb Farms recognizes that the RMP/PSM is a continuous process for evaluating, monitoring, and improving the handling of acutely / extremely hazardous chemicals and operations at its facility. As such, this document and related program elements will evolve as SupHerb Farms continue their ongoing focus and dedication of risk minimization and safety improvement for their employees and surrounding community. 

SupHerb Farms will submit revised information if a change occurs that is considered significant and requires resubmission under the regulations. However, minor improvements / modifications to the RMP/PSM, related attachments, and program elements will be incorporated consistently with SupHerb Farms's internal review practices, and SupHerb Farms will maintain the most current versions onsite. Thus, the most current version RMP/PSM an
d related documents and elements maintained onsite may vary slightly from the information in submittals made to EPA and other regulatory agencies.
